title: Tarapur Chemicals, Dyes & Intermediates: a note to the credit manager
narrative: **So when a proposal lands, check the working-capital cycle first, not the capex plan.** Where the receivable days and inventory days are not in the file, collect from customer.

## What has changed now
**The data call is Avoid (score 33), and the news flow is worse, so the call stays Avoid.** India-wide IIP for NIC 20 is -0.5% YoY and -1.2% Apr-to-date [D], while bank credit is +20.7% YoY [D] — money is chasing a shrinking output base. **Maharashtra electricity demand grew 6.0% Apr-to-date against India's 9.5% [D], a local demand signal that matters because power is a large running cost for these units.** Locally, a fire at a Tarapur MIDC mill ran two and a half hours before control, with financial loss reported [1]; a chemical plant explosion with casualties is reported nationally [3]. **So when a proposal lands, check the fire NOC, the last fire-audit date and the insurer's loading; if the audit is older than twelve months, ask for a fresh one before sanction.**

## Where the growth is
**Peer results show the demand is real for scale players: Aarti Industries reported Q2 FY27 net profit up 58.5% and revenue up 75% to ₹3,668 crore [6], with PAT at ₹169 crore on 30% volume growth [5] and record quarterly revenue and EBITDA [4][7].** That is export-led specialty volume, not commodity dye. **Pursue units with a written offtake or long-term supply agreement, own effluent treatment, and a product that is not a me-too colour.** Avoid traders with no plant, units with a single buyer above half of sales, and anyone whose fire compliance is unclear. **Rating commentary flags elevated working-capital intensity in high-growth chemical operations [9] and pricing pressure from Chinese dumping with inventory de-stocking abroad [8] — so ask for the buyer-wise sales split and the last price revision.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure on cash flow, not on the balance sheet: sanction against a drawing-power limit built on verified receivables, with a monthly stock-and-book-debt statement as the operating discipline.** Take the fire insurance assignment, a charge on receivables, and a promoter personal guarantee. **Take every month: stock statement, debtor ageing, power bill, and GST returns.** If the power bill shows a month-on-month fall beyond the seasonal norm, ask for the order book. **Rating reports note capex is largely met from internal accrual with minimal external funding [8] — so a borrower asking for term debt for expansion should show why internal accrual is insufficient.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the power bill, the fire audit and the debtor ageing together; they fail before the balance sheet does.** A falling power bill with flat sales means hidden shutdown; a lapsed fire NOC means the insurer can walk; a debtor list that lengthens by more than a fortnight means the buyer is squeezing. **If any two move together, stop fresh disbursement and ask for the buyer correspondence.**

older than twelve months or lapsed -> hold fresh disbursement until renewed
ageing lengthens by more than a fortnight -> ask for buyer correspondence and stop enhancement
